### Palindromes of length 3  

A 3‑character string is a palindrome iff its first and third characters are the same.

* **Letter part**  
  Choose the first letter (26 ways), the middle letter (26 ways), and the third must equal the first (1 way).  
  \[
  N_{\text{letter palindrome}} = 26\cdot 26 = 676 .
  \]

* **Digit part**  
  Choose the first digit (10 ways), the middle digit (10 ways), third equals the first.  
  \[
  N_{\text{digit palindrome}} = 10\cdot 10 = 100 .
  \]

### Plates with at least one palindrome

* \(A\): letter part is a palindrome.

\[
\begin{aligned}
P(A) &= \frac{676\cdot 10^{3}}{N_{\text{total}}}

P(B) &= \frac{26^{3}\cdot 100}{N_{\text{total}}}

P(A\cap B) &= \frac{676\cdot 100}{N_{\text{total}}}
            =\frac{67\,600}{17\,576\,000}.

Using inclusion–exclusion,

\[
P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)
